hook.text: The hunger of the famine year — the one the town survived by measures nobody names — has come back as weather: a thin wind that empties you however you eat, moving house to house down the same streets it worked twenty years ago, in the same order.
hook.pressure: The elders recognize the order and have started paying old debts at speed — bread on the doorsteps of families they shorted then, confessions at the rail — because the wind, it is now plain, lingers longest at the houses that fattened. The NPC's house is next on the old route, and the NPC's father kept the granary keys that year.
hook.ifIgnored: The wind arrives at the NPC's door and settles in — the whole inherited account presented at once — and the town watches the thinning like an augury. The wind will move on, the elders say, when the granary year is paid in full — and only the NPC's family ledger, kept in their father's careful hand, records how much that is, and from whom he took it.

rolled.calamity: The light has gone dark twice this month for reasons the keeper won't fully explain; a grain ship already broke up on the rocks during the second outage, and the salvage that washed ashore is being quietly kept rather than reported.
rolled.secret: The town charter included a provision for foundling care; the provision was quietly struck from the working copy seventy years ago; the original charter in the capital archive still has it.

Hometown: Coalstack Row: A terraced mining town where the houses climb the valley side in stairstep rows and every face is smudged black by noon. · Origin: A folk migration's far edge — they meant to go further, and didn't. · Myth: The Iron-Handed Knight: A local hero's prosthetic hand was blessed by a forge-god, and the hand — not the knight — won his duels. The smithy displays "the hand" (a hand; provenance negotiable), amputees come from three counties for prosthetics forged here, and the guild's oath is taken left-handed, the honest hand, "since the right one may have plans.".
The Archive-Brethren — the dominant power; means to win legitimacy — to be loved, not merely feared, through law, charters, and bureaucracy.
The Color-Miners — a rival (holding an uneasy truce); means to acquire one specific relic, secret, or person, through sabotage and accidents.

setup.skinVisual: Brickwork is blackened; mortar looks tar-stained.
setup.motifDesc: Cargo marks, guild stamps, registry seals. Points to a smuggler cache, counting house, or underworks link.
setup.motifModifierDesc: Rain/salt/soot/rust obscures it. Suggests drainage/airflow routes or hidden voids nearby.
setup.restDesc: Every creak sounded like footsteps. You cannot be surprised in the next segment.
setup.catalyst: A gang leader is executed in public (the manner is brutal; the crowd is silent throughout)
setup.distortionHow: Whoever was harmed is now suspected of having caused it — through recklessness, greed, or secret wickedness.
setup.distortionPrompt: *Why do locals distrust the victim? What evidence (real or imagined) supports their suspicion?*

skin.text: A cordon has appeared around a normally open building. — No explanation offered, guards who won't meet your eyes, and a queue of people trying to get information rather than entry.

segments.label: Spark
segments.description: Graves and crypts overflow; the dead rise confused or malevolent, filling streets and buildings.
segments.transition: 1: The undead target the living indiscriminately; flight is safer than fight. 2: A necromancer drives the dead toward specific locations or people. 3: The party discovers the rising serves a deeper purpose. 4: Holy ground or running water offers temporary refuge but not escape.

encounter.text: Enemy complication: Giant Spider (lurking in the rafters of an abandoned bell tower)

sceneFrame.tactical: Sinuous 10' curves with 6 gentle turns; sightline breaks.

dressing.text: Rubble slope that shifts under weight.

backgroundEvent.text: The Mind-Controlled Citizen: A completely blank-eyed commoner walks robotically into a brick wall, over and over, muttering praise to a hidden cult.

valuable.name: A clockwork songbird that sings only in total darkness
valuable.note: Wound in daylight it holds its peace; snuff the lamps and it starts mid-phrase. Toymakers will pay just to open it up.

segments.label: Escalation
segments.description: A volatile shop explodes in a sequence of cascading detonations, sending shrapnel and toxic fumes across a wide district.
segments.transition: 1: The blasts sever a bridge or collapse a building, cutting the city into hostile fragments. 2: Survivors are injured or mad; desperate for aid or turning violent from fear. 3: A faction claims the explosion was sabotage and blames someone the party knows. 4: The chaos reveals a secret cache or hidden passage buried in the rubble—but retrieving it means crossing dangerous debris.

encounter.text: A statue has moved from where it stood yesterday— not far, but visibly different location (the stonework shows no wear or disturbance)

dressing.text: Tally marks in different handwriting styles.

valuable.name: A pewter medallion of a minor local saint
valuable.note: Devotional, common in this region, worthless two towns over.

segments.label: Escalation
segments.description: Sickness spreads rapidly through a district; the infected become violent or catatonic, guards begin shooting anyone who flees.
segments.transition: 1: Quarantine lines cut off escape routes; immunity or disguise becomes essential. 2: The sick herd toward the party, exposing them as uninfected. 3: The disease spreads to the party, changing their situation fundamentally. 4: A faction offers aid—at the cost of the party's freedom or secrets.

encounter.text: A servant complains about the constant repairs at the city's east gate (three times in a month; the guards are unusually tight-lipped about it)

dressing.text: Tally marks in different handwriting styles.

backgroundEvent.text: Brush Seller: A patient craftswoman displays hand-bound scrub brushes and explains brush quality with unsettling intensity.

magic.name: Candle of the Deep
magic.desc: Burns for 8 hours without oxygen; cannot be extinguished by water or wind.

finale.revelation: An NPC the party trusted has been feeding false information — not from malice, but because they were deceived by someone higher up the food chain.
finale.exitState: Trust shatters like glass — neighbors eye each other with suspicion. The authority that was supposed to protect them failed. Informal networks form. People lock their doors. The community fractures.

rolled.setting: Coppice Rise: A wood-cutter's settlement in a managed forest, every able resident on rotation between the axe and the charcoal pit.
rolled.trait: The town sits at the confluence of two rivers; the point of land between them is the original settlement, the oldest buildings, and the most flood-prone ground.
rolled.calamity: Both rivers are running high simultaneously for the first time in a generation; the confluence point has been evacuated but several families refused to leave and cannot be reached.
rolled.secret: Three generations ago the miller's family was identified as lycanthropes; the council decided the mill was too important to lose and has been managing the full moons quietly ever since.
rolled.archetypeNote: Justice done fast and outdoors; the town remembers every name it has carried.

rolled.setting: The Quarantine Port: A harbor where incoming ships must anchor offshore for forty days before any cargo or passenger touches land.
rolled.trait: A great lighthouse on the headland is the town's reason for being and its largest public expense; the keeper's office is hereditary and the harbor dues that fund the light are the town's main revenue.
rolled.calamity: The light has gone dark twice this month for reasons the keeper won't fully explain; a grain ship already broke up on the rocks during the second outage, and the salvage that washed ashore is being quietly kept rather than reported.
rolled.secret: The town charter included a provision for foundling care; the provision was quietly struck from the working copy seventy years ago; the original charter in the capital archive still has it.
rolled.archetypeNote: The big shared machine — mill, dock, pump, reactor: what the place runs on.
